nodes.name: Schedule Trigger
nodes.notes: Fires the full sync + MCC account/campaign discovery chain automatically once a day at 6:00 AM server time (was previously an empty/unset interval, which likely wasn't firing reliably). Change daysInterval/triggerAtHour here, or edit directly in n8n's UI, to adjust the cadence.

nodes.name: Get all campaigns
nodes.notes: Confirmed live: zero campaigns (a fresh/empty campaigns table) halted the ENTIRE workflow here, including the unrelated MCC account-discovery branch downstream (Get all clients -> Get MCC accounts -> ...) since n8n stops executing when a node has no output data by default. alwaysOutputData fixes this the same way it was already fixed on 'Delete existing metrics row' and 'Delete existing open recommendations' elsewhere in this workflow. The single placeholder item this produces on a truly empty table is already handled safely by every downstream consumer (Filter buildable campaigns, Get distinct customers, Filter unknown accounts) since they all skip rows missing google_ads_customer_id.

nodes.name: Filter buildable campaigns
nodes.notes: Keeps only campaigns with both google_ads_customer_id and google_ads_campaign_resource set (i.e. actually built in Google Ads). One output item per valid campaign; the rest of this workflow processes each independently.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: `SELECT segments.date, metrics.cost_micros, metrics.conversions, metrics.conversions_value, metrics.impressions, metrics.clicks FROM campaign WHERE campaign.id = ${$json.googleCampaignId} AND segments.date DURING YESTERDAY` }) }}

nodes.name: Search campaign metrics
nodes.notes: Also switched to .first() (not .item) for 'Refresh Google Ads token' and 'Get Google Ads credentials' -- both are singleton nodes from well before any branching, but their .item reference can go ambiguous once an upstream node that manufactures new items (e.g. 'Filter buildable campaigns', or a multi-client 'Get all clients' feeding this node) produces 2+ items and breaks the automatic paired-item chain -- same root cause just fixed on 'Discover campaigns', proactively applied here before it causes the identical error live.

nodes.name: Build metrics row
nodes.notes:
Zero spend yesterday is a valid, common case — Google returns no rows for it, so this falls back to a zero-valued row rather than skipping the day (keeps daily history gap-free for charts).

Iterates all campaigns by index (matching 'Filter buildable campaigns' order to 'Search campaign metrics' order, both untouched between these two nodes so index alignment holds) — this Code node's default 'Run Once for All Items' mode does NOT automatically process one execution per campaign the way native nodes (HTTP/Supabase/IF) do; without this, only the first campaign in the account was ever synced.

nodes.name: Delete existing metrics row
nodes.notes:
Delete-then-create instead of upsert, since the native Supabase node's upsert support is unverified. Clears yesterday's row (if this campaign was already synced today) before inserting a fresh one — makes re-runs idempotent. The 'delete' operation itself is unverified against your instance; if its Field Name/ID dropdowns don't resolve, same fix pattern as everywhere else — tell me what the UI shows.

alwaysOutputData is on: n8n treats zero rows deleted (the normal, expected first-ever-run case) as zero output items and halts the whole workflow there otherwise — confirmed live ('No output data returned').

nodes.name: Get fresh recommendations
nodes.notes: Reads back what 'Create recommendation row' (the parallel branch below) just wrote. These two branches run concurrently with no explicit synchronization, so there's a small chance this reads slightly-stale recommendation data if the other branch hasn't finished yet — acceptable for a proactive nudge, not worth a Merge node's added complexity for this.

nodes.name: Build suggestion context
nodes.notes: Iterates all campaigns by index for metrics (index-matched, same reasoning as 'Build metrics row'), but matches recommendations by campaign_id rather than index — 'Get fresh recommendations' can return a different item shape per campaign (0+ rows each, though alwaysOutputData keeps it at 1 placeholder item minimum per campaign), so explicit campaign_id matching is safer than assuming index alignment survived.

parameters.text:
=Campaign: {{ $json.campaignName }} (status: {{ $json.status }}, daily budget ${{ $json.dailyBudgetUsd }}).
Yesterday ({{ $json.date }}): cost ${{ $json.cost }}, conversions {{ $json.conversions }}, conversion value ${{ $json.conversionsValue }}, ROAS {{ $json.roas || 'n/a' }}.

Open Google Ads recommendations:
{{ $json.recommendationsText }}

options.systemMessage:
You are reviewing this Google Ads campaign's daily performance sync automatically, on behalf of an agency, with no human having asked a question. Decide whether there's a genuinely useful, specific, non-obvious suggestion worth proactively surfacing right now — a real Google Ads recommendation with meaningful dollar impact, a clear problem (e.g. real spend with zero conversions), or a budget that's obviously binding. Be conservative: set should_post to false unless something actually stands out. Do not post just to have something to say — a missed useful suggestion is far better than noise the agency starts ignoring.

When should_post is true, proposed_action follows the same rules as elsewhere in this project: null UNLESS you're suggesting exactly one of update_daily_budget (daily_budget_usd required, a specific number), pause_campaign, or resume_campaign, with a one-sentence reason. Most suggestions will have proposed_action: null (e.g. flagging a recommendation the agency should look at manually in Google Ads) — only set an action when it's a clear, specific, agency-approvable change.

nodes.name: Suggest (AI Agent)
nodes.notes: onError is set to continueRegularOutput: confirmed live that the model occasionally returns a malformed structured output for one item (e.g. {output: null} instead of a filled-in object) on a sparse/edge-case campaign (paused, $0 everything) -- an LLM quirk, not something the prompt reliably prevents. Without this, one bad item halted the entire sync run's proactive-suggestion branch. 'Prepare suggestion' below now handles the resulting error/missing-output item defensively instead of crashing on it.

nodes.name: Prepare suggestion
nodes.notes: Iterates all campaigns by index, matching 'Suggest (AI Agent)' output items back to 'Build suggestion context' by position. UNVERIFIED assumption: that the AI Agent node processes multiple input items 1:1, preserving order, the same way native nodes do — I have no live access to confirm this for the LangChain agent node type specifically. If a second campaign's suggestion doesn't show up at all, or shows up with the wrong campaign's context, this is the node to check first. Confirmed live: the model sometimes returns {output: null} for one item (an LLM quirk on sparse campaigns, not a workflow bug) -- guarded against both that and an error-carrying item from the AI Agent's onError: continueRegularOutput setting, treating either as shouldPost: false instead of crashing on output.should_post.

nodes.name: Insert proactive suggestion
nodes.notes: Posts into the same campaign_chat_messages table CampaignChat.tsx reads — shows up in the Campaign Assistant tab exactly like a reply to a question, just unprompted. Confirm & Apply / Dismiss buttons work identically for these.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: `SELECT recommendation.resource_name, recommendation.type, recommendation.campaign, recommendation.impact FROM recommendation WHERE recommendation.campaign = 'customers/${$('Filter buildable campaigns').item.json.customerId}/campaigns/${$('Filter buildable campaigns').item.json.googleCampaignId}'` }) }}

nodes.name: Search recommendations
nodes.notes: Also switched to .first() (not .item) for 'Refresh Google Ads token' and 'Get Google Ads credentials' -- both are singleton nodes from well before any branching, but their .item reference can go ambiguous once an upstream node that manufactures new items (e.g. 'Filter buildable campaigns', or a multi-client 'Get all clients' feeding this node) produces 2+ items and breaks the automatic paired-item chain -- same root cause just fixed on 'Discover campaigns', proactively applied here before it causes the identical error live.

nodes.name: Delete existing open recommendations
nodes.notes:
Clears previously-open recommendations for this campaign before inserting the fresh set — correct behavior, not just idempotency: a recommendation Google Ads no longer surfaces should stop showing as 'open' here too. Does NOT touch rows already marked applied/dismissed.

alwaysOutputData is on: same zero-rows-halts-the-workflow issue confirmed live on the metrics branch's delete node — no open recommendations yet is the normal first-run case, not an error.

nodes.name: Build recommendation items
nodes.notes: Iterates all campaigns by index, flattening each campaign's recommendations into the output list. Can't use n8n's 'Run Once for Each Item' Code mode here since one campaign can produce 0-N recommendation items (that mode requires exactly 1 output per input) — explicit .all()-based iteration handles that correctly. Confirmed live: recommendation.impact (or its baseMetrics/potentialMetrics children) is missing entirely for some recommendation types -- crashed with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading baseMetrics)" as soon as a campaign had one of those. Both now default to an empty object so dollars_recoverable falls back to 0 instead of throwing. Confirmed live: recommendation.impact (or its baseMetrics/potentialMetrics children) is missing entirely for some recommendation types -- crashed with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading baseMetrics)" as soon as a campaign had one of those. Both now default to an empty object so dollars_recoverable falls back to 0 instead of throwing.

nodes.name: Create recommendation row
nodes.notes: Runs once per recommendation item from 'Build recommendation items' (n8n executes a node once per input item by default) — no bulk/array insert needed.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: `SELECT campaign.status, campaign_budget.amount_micros FROM campaign WHERE campaign.id = ${$('Filter buildable campaigns').item.json.googleCampaignId}` }) }}

nodes.name: Get campaign config
nodes.notes: Pulls the campaign's ACTUAL current status + budget from Google Ads, independent of how it got that way — catches changes made directly in the Google Ads UI, not just ones applied through apply-campaign-action.json/send-reply.json. Runs every sync, reconciling Supabase to reality rather than relying on every write path to remember to keep it in sync. Also switched to .first() (not .item) for 'Refresh Google Ads token' and 'Get Google Ads credentials' -- both are singleton nodes from well before any branching, but their .item reference can go ambiguous once an upstream node that manufactures new items (e.g. 'Filter buildable campaigns', or a multi-client 'Get all clients' feeding this node) produces 2+ items and breaks the automatic paired-item chain -- same root cause just fixed on 'Discover campaigns', proactively applied here before it causes the identical error live.

nodes.name: Build campaign config update
nodes.notes:
Maps Google's campaign.status enum (ENABLED/PAUSED/REMOVED/...) to this schema's values. Anything other than ENABLED/REMOVED falls back to 'paused' -- an unknown state should not read as 'active'. A campaign Google Ads no longer returns a row for, or explicitly reports as REMOVED, is routed to 'Removed in Google Ads?' for deletion from Supabase instead of a config update, so a campaign deleted directly in the Google Ads UI disappears from the dashboard on the next sync rather than sitting there stale forever.

Iterates all campaigns by index, same reason as 'Build metrics row' above.

nodes.name: Update campaign config
nodes.notes: Reconciles Supabase's status + daily_budget_usd to whatever Google Ads actually reports right now — this is what makes the dashboard trustworthy even for changes made outside this app entirely.

nodes.name: Get distinct customers
nodes.notes: One item per distinct google_ads_customer_id already known to Supabase, carrying every already-tracked campaign resource name so 'Filter new campaigns' can tell what's genuinely new vs. already imported. Skips any customer_id shared by more than one client entirely, rather than guessing which client owns a newly-discovered campaign for it — confirmed live that guessing wrong is a real failure mode, not just theoretical.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: `SELECT campaign.id, campaign.name, campaign.status, campaign.resource_name, campaign_budget.amount_micros, campaign_budget.resource_name FROM campaign WHERE campaign.status != 'REMOVED'` }) }}

nodes.name: Discover campaigns
nodes.notes: Uses .first() (not .item) for 'Refresh Google Ads token' and 'Get Google Ads credentials' -- both always produce exactly one item, from well before any of the three discovery sources branch off, but n8n's pairedItem tracking can't resolve .item once one of those sources (e.g. 'Get clients pending discovery', which builds brand-new JSON objects via .map()) loses the automatic paired-item link back to them. Confirmed live: '.item' errored with "Paired item data ... is unavailable" as soon as 'Get clients pending discovery' produced more than one item.

nodes.name: Filter new campaigns
nodes.notes: 'Discover campaigns' has THREE upstream sources ('Get distinct customers', 'Prepare for campaign discovery', 'Get clients pending discovery') and any subset of them can produce items in the same run. Matches each HTTP response back to its customer context by customerId parsed out of the response's own campaign.resourceName, NOT by array index -- confirmed live that index-based pairing broke as soon as two sources produced items in the same run simultaneously (a client with existing tracked campaigns via 'Get distinct customers' running alongside a brand-new client-level-customer-id client via 'Get clients pending discovery'), since it depends on n8n's actual multi-source merge order matching the concatenation order here, which isn't guaranteed and evidently didn't hold.

nodes.name: Insert discovered campaign
nodes.notes: primary_keyword/goal are intentionally left unset (now nullable) — those are intake-form concepts that don't apply to a campaign nobody built through this app. Shows up on the dashboard exactly like any other campaign once inserted; the next sync run's metrics/recommendations/config branches will pick it up too since they iterate every campaign with a google_ads_campaign_resource, not just ones from the intake flow. continueOnFail is on so a unique-constraint conflict (campaigns_google_ads_campaign_resource_uidx, added after a live duplicate-insert race condition was found) skips just that one duplicate item instead of halting the whole sync run.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ query: `SELECT customer_client.id, customer_client.descriptive_name FROM customer_client WHERE customer_client.manager = false AND customer_client.status = 'ENABLED'` }) }}

nodes.name: Get MCC accounts
nodes.notes: Asks the MCC directly what real, enabled client accounts it manages — not derived from anything already in Supabase. This is what catches an account like a newly-linked client that has no clients/campaigns row yet at all. Also switched to .first() (not .item) for 'Refresh Google Ads token' and 'Get Google Ads credentials' -- both are singleton nodes from well before any branching, but their .item reference can go ambiguous once an upstream node that manufactures new items (e.g. 'Filter buildable campaigns', or a multi-client 'Get all clients' feeding this node) produces 2+ items and breaks the automatic paired-item chain -- same root cause just fixed on 'Discover campaigns', proactively applied here before it causes the identical error live.

nodes.name: Filter unknown accounts
nodes.notes: Keeps only MCC-managed accounts with zero campaigns rows in Supabase. For each one, also checks whether a client row already exists for it (matched via the googleads-<id>@discovered.local placeholder email pattern 'Create client for discovered account' uses) — existingClientId is set if so, so 'Client already exists?' downstream can skip creating a duplicate and just retry campaign discovery for the existing client instead.

nodes.name: Create client for discovered account
nodes.notes: Auto-onboards a real Google Ads account found under the MCC as a client row so its campaigns have somewhere to attach to. The email is a clearly-fake placeholder (googleads-<id>@discovered.local) since there's no real contact info to use — there's no 'edit client' UI yet, so replace it directly in Supabase once you know who this account actually belongs to.

nodes.name: Prepare for campaign discovery
nodes.notes: Reshapes into the same {customerId, clientId, loginCustomerId, knownResources} shape 'Get distinct customers' produces. clientId prefers source.existingClientId (set when a client already existed for this account) over $json.id (the freshly-created client row's id) — covers both the 'brand new account' and 'client exists, campaigns just never got discovered' cases with one node.

nodes.name: Sync Now Webhook
nodes.notes: Called by the dashboard's "Sync Now" button. Runs the exact same flow as the daily Schedule Trigger — both feed into "Get Google Ads credentials". Responds immediately (onReceived) rather than waiting for the whole sync to finish, since this can involve several Google Ads API calls per campaign; the dashboard just reloads its data a few seconds after firing this, best-effort.

nodes.name: Get all clients
nodes.notes: Needed so 'Filter unknown accounts' can recognize an account that already has a client row but zero campaigns yet (e.g. a previous sync created the client but discovery failed before finding its campaigns) — without this, every such account would get a DUPLICATE client row created on every subsequent sync, since the old check only looked at campaigns.google_ads_customer_id. Also needs alwaysOutputData: true for the same reason as 'Get all campaigns' above — zero clients (a fresh/empty clients table) would otherwise halt the workflow here too, before 'Get MCC accounts' ever runs. The placeholder item this produces on an empty table is already handled safely (Filter unknown accounts only matches clients whose email fits the googleads-<id>@discovered.local pattern). executeOnce is on: this node was running once PER INPUT ITEM (n8n's default for any node), and it's fed by Get all campaigns which now has multiple items (one per real campaign) -- confirmed live it ran 3 times and produced 6 duplicated client rows (2 real clients x 3), which cascaded into Get clients pending discovery incorrectly treating one real client as multiple ambiguous ones sharing a customer_id and skipping it. This node never needed per-item context (it just fetches the whole clients table), so it should only ever run once per sync.

nodes.name: Get clients pending discovery
nodes.notes: Catches a client whose google_ads_customer_id was set directly on the CLIENT row (via the New Client / Edit Client forms) but who has zero campaigns yet — 'Get distinct customers' can't find these (it only derives customer IDs from existing campaign rows, so a client with no campaigns has nothing for it to read), and 'Get MCC accounts' only finds accounts that are real linked children of the MCC, which excludes direct-access accounts like 3534195221 entirely. Without this branch, such a client's campaigns would never be auto-discovered at all — confirmed live: a client created with a manually-entered Customer ID stayed at 0 campaigns through every sync. Confirmed live: two clients ended up with the same google_ads_customer_id set (both with zero campaigns) -- without this guard, both got emitted as separate items with the same customerId, and 'Filter new campaigns' (which maps by customerId) silently collapsed them into one entry, attributing every discovered campaign to whichever client happened to be last rather than the one the agency actually meant. Now matches 'Get distinct customers'' existing skip-on-ambiguity behavior instead of guessing.

nodes.name: Get recent suggestions
nodes.notes: Fetches this campaign's past proactive-suggestion messages so 'Filter should post (dedupe)' can tell whether posting a new one would just be a repeat. alwaysOutputData is on since a campaign with no prior suggestions (the normal case) returns zero rows, which would otherwise halt the workflow here.

nodes.name: Filter should post (dedupe)
nodes.notes: Confirmed live: without this, the same $0-budget/$0-spend campaign got a fresh near-duplicate budget-change suggestion posted on every single sync run (auto-sync-on-load + schedule + manual Sync Now all compound this), since the AI Agent has no memory of what it already suggested. Suppresses should_post when an unresolved actionable suggestion is already sitting in the thread, or any suggestion for this campaign was posted within the last 24 hours.

nodes.name: Delete removed campaign
nodes.notes: Cascades to campaign_metrics/recommendations/campaign_chat_messages via their FK on_delete cascade -- matches the same cleanup delete-campaign.json does for an agency-initiated delete.
